Here's my detailed review, including both its strengths and weaknesses: Pros: Build and Comfort: The neckband design is light, comfortable, and skin-friendly. It doesn’t feel like a burden even after wearing it all day. The IP55 rating adds durability, making it resistant to sweat and dust. Sound Performance: The 12.4mm drivers deliver impressive bass-heavy audio. If you enjoy bass-focused music, these earphones will suit your taste. Call quality is also commendable, with clear audio and passive noise cancellation. Battery Life: The battery life is excellent, easily lasting multiple days on moderate use. Quick charging is another highlight, providing hours of playback after just a few minutes of charging. Ease of Pairing: Connecting the earbuds is simple and quick. They pair automatically with the phone once you put them on, adding convenience. Cons: Lack of Dual Pairing: The absence of dual-device connectivity can be frustrating, especially when switching between devices like a phone and laptop. Unintended Connection Issues: When the earbuds are magnetically connected, they switch off. However, if they separate accidentally (e.g., in a bag), they reconnect automatically, draining the battery and muting phone notifications. Sound Profile Imbalance: While the bass is strong, the audio lacks balance, which can disappoint those who prefer clear mids and highs, especially for classical or melodious music. Control Button Chaos: The multi-function button for play/pause, calls, and track changes can be confusing and unintuitive, requiring precise presses for different actions. Not Ideal for All Activities: These earphones are uncomfortable when used with a helmet and may fall out during intense gym sessions. Final Thoughts: The OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 excels in its build quality, bass-heavy sound, and long-lasting battery life, making it suitable for casual music listeners and travelers. However, its lack of dual pairing, occasional connection issues, and imbalanced sound profile may deter audiophiles and multitaskers. If you're looking for reliable, budget-friendly earphones and prioritize bass over balance, these are worth considering. However, if you're seeking a more versatile experience, you might want to explore alternatives

OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 Review: Battery King with Bombastic Bass The OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 continues the tradition of the brand's popular neckband earphones, delivering exceptional value, especially for users who prioritize battery life and a bass-forward sound signature. If you're looking for a reliable, all-day companion for music and calls, this is an excellent choice. What Stands Out (The Good) Exceptional Battery Life & Warp Charge: This is the headline feature. The Bullets Wireless Z2 offers a staggering up to 30 hours of playback on a single charge. Even better is the speed: a quick 10-minute charge can give you up to 20 hours of listening time. For heavy users, this feature alone is a game-changer. Powerful, Bass-Heavy Sound: Thanks to the large 12.4mm dynamic drivers, these earphones deliver a sonic experience that is punchy, loud, and undeniably bass-heavy. Genres like EDM, pop, and hip-hop really shine, providing a deep, thumping low-end that many users love. The sound is designed to be energetic and exciting, easily cutting through noisy environments. Durability and Comfort: With an IP55 rating, the earphones are protected against dust and sweat, making them perfect for workouts, commutes, or use in light rain. The neckband itself is comfortable, made of a skin-friendly silicone material that's great for all-day wear. Clear Call Quality: The built-in AI Noise Cancellation technology for calls works well to dynamically reduce ambient noise, keeping your voice clean and clear for the person on the other end, even when you are outdoors. Convenient Features: The familiar magnetic control for power (separating the buds turns them on, clipping them together turns them off) is a handy, intuitive feature. Quick pairing with OnePlus phones is also seamless. Areas for Consideration Bass Can Be Overpowering: While the powerful bass is a pro for many, it can be a con for audiophiles or those who prefer a more neutral sound profile. In certain tracks, the bass can be so strong that it overshadows the mid-range and treble, potentially becoming fatiguing over long listening sessions. No Active Noise Cancellation (ANC): Unlike the Z2 ANC variant, this model relies solely on passive noise isolation from the eartips. While the loud volume helps in noisy places, dedicated ANC is a feature some users might miss. Codec Support: The earphones support standard SBC and AAC codecs. While adequate for most people, they lack support for higher-resolution codecs like aptX, which can limit audio quality for listeners with high-end source devices. Verdict The OnePlus Bullets Wireless Z2 are designed to be the ultimate value-for-money neckband for the masses. They are a clear winner for anyone seeking unmatched battery performance and a fun, bass-forward sound that makes your music pop. If your primary concerns are all-day power, good call quality, and gym-readiness without spending a fortune, the Bullets Wireless Z2 should be at the very top of your list.

Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra – Excellent Upgrade from S22 Ultra I moved to the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra after using the S22 Ultra for almost 4 years. Unfortunately, my S22 Ultra suddenly stopped working one day, don't know the reason of the damage, so I had to replace it and decided to go with the S25 Ultra. After using the S25 Ultra, I can confidently say that the upgrade has been excellent. The first thing I noticed is the weight and feel of the phone. Although it has a large 6.9-inch display and a 5,000 mAh battery, it feels noticeably lighter and more comfortable than my S22 Ultra. Samsung lists the S25 Ultra at 218 g, compared with 229 g for the S22 Ultra. What I like most 1\. Customization – Excellent This is probably the thing I like most about Samsung phones. The level of customization available is incredible. You can customize the home screen, lock screen, widgets, themes, icons, gestures, Edge panels, Always-On Display and many other aspects. There is almost no limit to how much you can personalize the phone. This is one area where I feel Samsung is far ahead of many other smartphones. 2\. Display – Excellent The display is absolutely beautiful. It is crisp, bright and smooth, and the 120 Hz refresh rate makes everything feel very fluid. The 6.9-inch QHD+ Dynamic AMOLED 2X display is one of the biggest strengths of the phone. 3\. Sound – Very good The speaker quality is also very impressive. Music, YouTube, calls and videos sound clear and powerful for a smartphone. 4\. Performance – Excellent Coming from the S22 Ultra, the S25 Ultra feels significantly faster and smoother in everyday use. Apps open quickly, multitasking is excellent and the phone handles demanding applications without any noticeable slowdown. Samsung uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite for Galaxy, along with an improved cooling system, which helps with sustained performance. 5\. Camera – Excellent The camera system is another major improvement. The 200 MP main camera and the new 50 MP ultra-wide camera provide excellent detail and versatility. Samsung has also improved night photography and video processing. 6\. S Pen S Pen – One Step Back from S22 Ultra The S Pen is still one of the unique advantages of the Ultra series, and I use it regularly for notes, screenshots, editing and precise interaction with the phone. However, this is one area where I feel the S25 Ultra is actually a downgrade compared with my S22 Ultra. My S22 Ultra S Pen had Bluetooth and Air Actions, which meant I could use the S Pen as a remote shutter button for the camera. I especially used this feature for group selfies and taking photos from a distance. It was genuinely useful and one of the features I loved about the S Pen. Unfortunately, the S25 Ultra S Pen no longer has Bluetooth, so the remote camera shutter and Air Actions are no longer available. For me, this is a significant miss. Samsung has improved the phone in many areas, but removing a useful feature that was already available on the S22 Ultra feels like a step backwards. I really hope Samsung brings Bluetooth and remote-camera functionality back to the S Pen in future Ultra models. One disappointment – Amazon sale pricing The one thing I was not happy about was the Amazon sale pricing. I was monitoring the phone price before purchasing. Just one day before the sale, the price was around ₹89,899. On the actual sale day, the price increased to ₹94,999, and then the exchange offer was presented as an additional benefit. This made me question the actual value of the so-called sale. In my experience, the sale did not feel like a genuine special offer, because the price was actually lower before the sale started. Customers who track prices can easily notice this. I would therefore recommend that buyers check the price history for a few days before purchasing during an Amazon sale, rather than assuming that the displayed "sale price" is necessarily the best price. Overall Coming from an S22 Ultra that I used for nearly four years, I am very happy with the S25 Ultra.
